This after-action debrief documents a closed exercise in which the actor engaged in insurance fraud, including fabricating a workplace injury, coaching witnesses, and altering medical records to deceive an insurer. The artifacts include false injury reports, scripted testimonies, altered clinical notes, and a defense brief filed in the exercise records. Critical checks skipped include verification of incident timestamps, independent witness confirmation, due diligence on healthcare compliance, fact-checking before submission, right to counsel notification, consistency review, obtaining proper legal representation, full disclosure of materials to investigators, forensic review of data alterations, and mandatory conflict-of-interest disclosures to licensing boards. This scenario represents a serious violation of law and professional ethics; in a real context, it would constitute fraud, criminal conspiracy, and professional misconduct warranting immediate legal, administrative, and potential criminal action.
